title: taskloom Configuration
description: Schema for taskloom's own config.yaml files (~/.taskloom/config.yaml and the per-project .taskloom/config.yaml), layered via internal/shared/confload exactly like ctxloom's own config-schema.json.

homing.description: Where the project's task-store log is homed. "home" keeps it PRIVATE under ~/.ctxloom/tasks/<project-id>.jsonl (today's default behavior; never committed, never shared by a clone). "repo" checks the log into the project tree at .taskloom/tasks.jsonl, alongside this config file, so it is SHAREABLE and travels with clones. taskloom refuses to guess: this key (at either the home or project config layer), the TASKLOOM_CONFIG_HOMING environment variable, or the --homing flag must set it before any command that touches a single project's store will run.

tag_schema.description: Tag-schema declarations, each written in tagma's own tag syntax, asserting a facet over a tag key used on this project's tasks — e.g. `tagma.arity:"triage:type"=scalar`. Today only the `arity` facet is enforced: a target declared `=scalar` may carry at most one tag with that (namespace, key) per task, and taskloom's write seam collapses a re-tag onto it (the newest value survives; the log still records both the retracting untag and the new tag, so history is never rewritten) — see internal/shared/tasks/tagschema and internal/shared/tasks/operations. `tagma.priority_fn:"<key>"="<mustache-equation>"` and `tagma.decay_fn:"<key>"="<mustache-equation>"` declarations are parsed and stored but not yet evaluated (a later ranking feature). This key replaces the WHOLE list at whichever layer sets it last (home < project < TASKLOOM_CONFIG_* env < --config-set) — it is never merged element-by-element. Unset at every layer falls back to taskloom's built-in triage-classification baseline: `triage:type` and `triage:impact` declared scalar, plus that baseline's own priority_fn/decay_fn declarations for `triage:impact`.
